questions.q: Which journal sources should be reviewed for unposted or error status before closing a period?
options: Only manual journals; imported and recurring journals cannot have this issue
Manual journals, imported journals, and recurring or allocation journals — any source can have unposted or error journals
Only journals created in the current fiscal year
Only journals above a certain dollar threshold
questions.explain: Any journal source — manual, imported, recurring, or allocation — can end up stuck unposted or in error, so the review must cover all of them.

questions.q: In the LTV Manufacturing Corporation example, why is JE-10428 (a recurring journal) still unposted?
options: Because recurring journals can never be posted
Because generating a recurring journal does not automatically post it — it still needs to be submitted
Because it failed account validation
Because it is awaiting approval
questions.explain: Recurring journal generation (Chapter 4) only creates the journal; it still must be submitted for posting separately.

questions.q: What is a common reason a journal shows an Error status rather than Unposted?
options: It was created too early in the period
It failed validation, for example referencing an invalid account combination
It was approved too quickly
It used the wrong currency symbol only, with no other issue
questions.explain: An Error status typically indicates the journal failed validation, such as an invalid account combination, and cannot post until corrected.

questions.q: What happens to a period's final numbers if an unposted journal is left unresolved when the period closes?
options: Oracle Fusion automatically posts it to the closed period anyway
That journal's activity is simply not included in the period's final numbers, requiring posting elsewhere or a disruptive reopen later
The journal is permanently deleted
The period automatically reopens itself every night until it is posted
questions.explain: Closing a period does not resolve pending journals; their activity is excluded from that period's final balances unless addressed through other means.

questions.q: Why is clearing unposted and error journals before close considered cheaper than discovering them after?
options: Because journals cannot be edited after a period closes without potentially needing to reopen the period, which is itself disruptive
Because journals are automatically deleted once a period closes
Because closed periods process faster than open ones
Because there is no actual cost difference
questions.explain: Addressing missing journals after close may require reopening the period, which carries its own disruption, making proactive review before close the cheaper path.
